security_findings.finding: RESOLVED (was medium in round 1): _iter_files_recursive() now accepts a timed_out list mutable signal, records start_time once at entry, and checks elapsed time against the 10s timeout at the top of every _walk() call (file_search.py lines 55-64), once per directory visited, BEFORE folder.iterdir() runs, not just inside the content-read loop. When the budget is exceeded it sets timed_out[0]=True and returns without recursing further, so partially-discovered files up to that point are still yielded. search_files() creates discovery_timed_out=[False], passes it into _iter_files_recursive, and seeds partial = discovery_timed_out[0] (file_search.py lines 198-199, 249) BEFORE the content_contains loop even starts, so a metadata-only search (no content_contains) on a huge or slow tree now correctly surfaces partial=True instead of hanging silently forever. The content-search loop can still only turn partial True, never back to False, preserving OR-semantics across both timeout sources. This closes the exact gap identified in round 1.
security_findings.scenario: Verified with the new TestSearchFilesDiscoveryTimeoutWithoutContentContains test: monkeypatches time.monotonic to jump 11s ahead after the first call, calls search_files with name_contains set to file and return_partial=True, with NO content_contains argument, and asserts partial is True. This is precisely the previously-unprotected code path.

alternative_approach.recommended_direction: No architectural change recommended this round; the fix directly implements the exact direction proposed in round 1: push the same 10s deadline check into _iter_files_recursive itself, checked once per directory visited.
alternative_approach.rationale: The round-1 proposal has been implemented as specified; no further direction change is warranted for this specific finding. The remaining low-severity cycle-protection observation could be revisited in a future round if diamond-shaped symlink topologies become a real user scenario, but is not urgent enough to block this task.

approved_points: Discovery-phase timeout check happens before folder.iterdir() runs for each directory, not after enumerating entries, so a single pathologically large directory is still bounded by the per-directory check timing.

The mutable list-based timed_out signal correctly propagates across recursive _walk() generator calls without needing nonlocal or global state, and is checked both at function entry and mid-loop, so timeout detection latency is at most one directory-entries-iteration.
partial=True is OR-combined across discovery-timeout and content-timeout sources, preserving the existing content-timeout semantics while adding the new discovery-timeout source cleanly.
New test isolates the exact previously-unprotected scenario rather than just re-testing the already-covered content_contains timeout path.
Full test suite run independently by this reviewer confirms 350 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed, no regressions introduced by the fix.
overall_assessment: The round-1 medium-severity finding (unbounded pure-discovery walk when content_contains is omitted) is CONFIRMED FIXED. _iter_files_recursive() now takes a 10s time budget checked once per directory visited, signals timeout back to search_files() via a mutable timed_out list, and search_files() seeds partial=True from this signal unconditionally. A new, correctly-isolated test locks in this behavior without content_contains present. Full backend test suite re-run by this reviewer independently: 350 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed. The remaining round-1 low-severity finding (flat cycle-protection visited-set) was not re-reviewed in depth this round and remains an accepted, non-blocking observation.
